words.unsupported-by-counterpart: the Maestro consumer exists and refuses; the producer is one the counterpart owes (owner mega-maestro, named by dependency) and has not published; a managed caller refuses and never falls back to standalone, and negotiation reports the row by this name instead of activating

harness.note: inline Node program under --permission, admitted at the real spawn with declared read-only inputs and a private work directory

enforcement.files: read: the declared inputs only; write: the work directory only; anything else ERR_ACCESS_DENIED
enforcement.network: denied: no --allow-net, so connect and listen fail with ERR_ACCESS_DENIED
enforcement.descendants: denied: no --allow-child-process or --allow-worker, so none can start
enforcement.environment: complete, not inherited: PATH and HOME only

harness.qualifies: exactly this: a synthetic Node program launched through the protected dispatch on this host
harness.doesNotQualify: any real provider (Claude, Codex, OpenCode or another), anything a provider starts, or the Node permission model as an OS boundary

readings: managed: implemented on child-process is the launch admitted at the real spawn, not the provider: tool, file and network effects of a real provider are unqualified
hermes reads implemented from the capability table, but planSessionTurn refuses it with no-parser, so no Hermes turn runs on any surface

an enrolled installation with the reviewed endpoint refuses every real launch as unavailable (effect authority and delegation producers absent: CP-01, CP-03); only the synthetic harness route runs end to end
ssh stays unsupported until a remote attests a registered authority with managed: implemented on its own ssh row; no build of this version does

platform: identity custody needs Electron safeStorage or an equivalent protected seal; a plain Node host (maestro-cli host) composes no managed standing
